sections.html:
Dalton anchors Whitfield County, with Cohutta, Tunnel Hill and Varnell as the other cities, all settled along rail lines. The July 2025 estimate is 106,212 residents on 290.45 square miles of land. The midpoint owner-occupied home is worth $218,000, and 67.0% of the 40,987 housing units are owner-occupied.

  • Median rent: $971. Permits issued during 2025: 409.
  • Households: 36,834, averaging 2.78 people. Median household income: $67,070.

Whitfield has designated historic sites, and a parcel inside one faces design review. Before listing land near Rocky Face Ridge or Prater's Mill, ask the county planning office whether the lot lies inside a designated area.

sections.h2: Who sends the bill, and when?
sections.html:
Visit 1013 Riverburch Parkway, Dalton, GA 30721, or phone (706) 275-7510 any weekday from 8:00 to 4:55. Online payment has its own county tax site. The Board of Assessors, which sets valuation, keeps a separate tax help site that the county's home page links.

Real property bills typically go out in October and rest on the market value as of each January 1. The usual real estate due date is December 20, but your own bill is what counts. A mobile home is billed in January with April 1 as the deadline.

Owners inside Dalton face one extra wrinkle. The county assesses at 40% of market value and Dalton does so at 100%. A house inside Dalton therefore carries a different base than one in the unincorporated county, and the commissioner can tell you which levies reach your address.

Each month's interest is the prime rate plus 3 points, taken on January 1 and divided by 12.

A penalty of 5% is added each 120 days of delinquency up to a ceiling of 20%. At 120 days the commissioner files a lien against the property and the owner with the Clerk of Court and on the General Execution Docket, adding fees of $12 and $10. These liens are public, so credit bureaus may read them.

Whitfield gives you 45 days from the notice date to put an appeal on paper. Value, uniformity, taxability and a denied exemption count as grounds, while the size of the bill does not. Send it to the Board of Tax Assessors and name the track you want.

Three tracks are open to you. The county equalization board is the usual one. A hearing officer handles just non-homestead real estate above $500,000, while arbitration depends on a certified appraisal you pay for. Superior court is the last step, reached by written notice within 30 days of the decision. The state revenue department cannot overrule a county board on one parcel.

From January 1 to April 1 you may file a return with a value of your own. If you say nothing, last year's final value carries over, and the assessors mail business and personal property return forms each January. For a mobile home, the tax bill itself serves as the assessment notice and its 45 days run from the mailing date.

Qualifying takes ownership plus residence on January 1. The Tax Assessor takes the form, and one that arrives after April 1 is credited to the following year. An approved exemption renews itself unless you move or request another type. Five codes apply.

  • S1: regular homestead, with no extra conditions.
  • S1-V: regular homestead plus a City of Varnell exemption, for age 65 and income over $40,000.
  • S3: senior homestead at 65 with spousal income under $40,000.
  • S4-7: senior homestead at age 70.
  • S5: disabled veteran exemption, requiring a DD-214 and a 100% disability rating.

An owner who turns 62 can ask about one more exemption. Special assessment programs cover conservation use, residential transitional property, agriculture, rehabilitated historic buildings, qualified timber and the Forest Land Protection Act. Each requires an application and a commitment to keep the property in that use for a set number of years.

The January 1 owner's name goes on the statement. The office does not decide who owes what once a house sells; buyers and sellers typically work that out at closing. Where the office learns of a sale within 90 days of the due date and verifies the transfer, a bill goes to the new owner.

The owner of record changes once the deed is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. Lenders are not sent the bill, so a seller who escrows should tell the loan servicer. Request a balance covering earlier years and ask whether city levies for Dalton or Varnell apply.

Order of work: get the written balance, confirm your exemption with the assessors, record the deed, and give the figures to the closing attorney. A cash buyer taking the house as is lets the county be paid at the table. That suits an inherited house or a rental with several years open, and it spares you a repair list.

sections.h2: What to bring and what to ask
sections.html:
At the Riverburch Parkway office, bring the parcel number or the name on the bill. Ask for the balance for every open year, and ask whether the figure holds through your closing date, since interest is added monthly. If a mobile home sits on the land, ask for its account separately because it follows the January and April 1 calendar.

At the assessors, confirm that your homestead code is on file and that the acreage and building details are right. Before writing an appeal, gather nearby sales of similar houses and any repair quotes, and keep a copy of what you mail.

Out-of-town owners can do nearly all of this by phone, and payment itself goes through the county's online tax site, so nobody has to drive to Dalton. Whitfield's mix of in-town houses, mill-era neighborhoods and rural lots means two sellers can face quite different bills, so check your own parcel rather than a neighbor's. Have staff confirm every payoff figure in writing so the closing attorney holds it on paper, and note the date and the name of the person who gave it to you.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Whitfield County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: The main office is at 1013 Riverburch Parkway, Dalton, Georgia 30721. Call (706) 275-7510 on a weekday between eight and 4:55.

faqs.q: How soon must I contest a Whitfield County value?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice, in writing, to the Board of Tax Assessors, naming the method you choose. The tax amount itself cannot be appealed.

faqs.q: Does the City of Dalton assess differently from the county?
faqs.a: Yes. The county uses 40% of market value and the City of Dalton uses 100%. Ask which one reaches your address.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for a Whitfield County homestead form?
faqs.a: It must be received before April 1 of the tax year to count for that year. Later forms apply to the following year, and you need to own and occupy the home on January 1.

faqs.q: Who pays if I sell partway through the year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner receives the statement, and buyer and seller typically settle it at closing. Notice of the sale within 90 days of the due date lets the office bill the new owner. Lenders are not mailed a copy.
